body.statement:
Fix a positive observed binary law \(P\) and finite \(G,B,C\geq 1\).  Under target-strategy consistency, Tan's Lemmas 7--8 imply the following two facts.  First, a triple \((\lambda _1,\lambda _{0Y},\lambda _{0L})\) is induced by a full-data law compatible with the complete observed marginal \(P\) if and only if it belongs to \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\).  Second, after writing \(s_\ell=p_\ell\lambda _1(\ell,1)\), \(r_\ell=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)s_\ell\), \(t_\ell=r_\ell\lambda _{0Y}(\ell,1)\), and \(h=q_0\lambda _{0L}(0)\), the compatible law has
\[
 \mathbb E[Y^{1,1}]
 =a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell r_\ell
 +(1-a)\{h t_0+(1-h)t_1\}.
\]
Conversely, every value of this display generated by a ratio triple in \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\) is attained by such a compatible full-data law.

source.locator: Section 3.3, Lemma 7, equations (32)--(35), and Lemma 8, equations (37)--(38)
source.verbatim_statement: Conversely, if nonnegative functions $\lambda_1 (\overline{L}_1, y)$, $\lambda_{0,Y} (L_0, l_1, y)$, and $\lambda_{0,L_1} (L_0, l_1)$ satisfy [the displayed normalization constraints], then there exists a probability distribution $Q$ for the full data $(\overline{A}_1, L_0,\{(L_1^{a_0a_1},Y^{a_0a_1}): a_0,a_1=0,1\} )$ satisfying the two properties: (i) the induced distribution of $Q$ on the observed data $(\overline{A}_1,\overline{L}_1,Y )$ under Assumption A1$^\dag$ coincides with the true distribution of $(\overline{A}_1,\overline{L}_1,Y )$, (ii) $\lambda^*_{1,Q}=\lambda_1$, $\lambda^*_{0,Y,Q}=\lambda_{0,Y}$, and $\lambda^*_{0,L_1,Q}=\lambda_{0,L_1}$. The sharp upper bound $\mu^{1,1}_{+,\mathrm{Prod}}$ in (37) can be equivalently obtained as the maximum of the ICE, equivalently IPW, functional over all nonnegative functions subject to the normalization constraints (32)--(35) and the range constraints (38).
